summary: Hard slug-level claim lock added to /z-plan and /z-audit-plan setup to prevent silent double-work by concurrent sessions. scripts/plan-claim.sh is a non-interactive wrapper over sink-lock.sh; lock path is <base>/active-plans/claims/<slug>.lock via plan-path.sh:claims_dir(). Orthogonal to the lockless awareness registry (Invariant 1): registry stays advisory-only, claim lock is a hard mutex. Holder string: <session_id>::<run_id>::<command>; parsed by splitting on first+second '::' only. Claim-first ordering (Invariant 2): acquire before run-brief init, before register, before any artifact write. Session-id persist+restore (Invariant 7): persisted to archive/$RUN/session-id, restored on resume before acquire, so self-reentry guard works cross-resume on macOS. Exit-code contract: acquire 0=acquired/self-reentry/disabled, 1=live-peer (holder JSON stdout, TOCTOU/display-only), 2=stale-takeover (we hold), 3=corrupt; heartbeat 9=confirmed-lost-claim (ownership-change only; transient read error is NOT 9 — emits heartbeat_error + exit 0); release always 0 (best-effort). Post-crash daemon leak: the setsid-detached daemon survives SIGKILL and leaks until next same-slug acquire's TTL-takeover (or reboot); exit-2 is the normal crash-recovery path; unattended exit-2 default-aborts unless Z_HARNESS_CLAIM_OVERRIDE=1. Env knobs (all env-only, not TOML keys): Z_HARNESS_CLAIM_TTL_SECS (2700), Z_HARNESS_CLAIM_OVERRIDE (unattended proceed override), Z_HARNESS_CLAIM_DISABLE=1 (escape hatch, all subcommands exit-0 no-op; release is safe no-op without event-presence gate). Manual unlock: rm <claims_dir>/<slug>.lock <claims_dir>/<slug>.lock.hb.lock.
invariants: The lockless awareness registry (active-plan-registry.py) stays ADVISORY. The claim lock is a SEPARATE hard lock. Claim acquire/heartbeat/release MUST NEVER write a peer's registry record. The registry's overlap output is NEVER a hard gate. (Invariant 1)
Claim acquire is the FIRST action after slug+run-id resolution — before run-brief init, before register, before any artifact write. (Invariant 2)
No reliance on a cross-call EXIT trap. Hard-kill recovery is guaranteed only by release on every halt-finalize path + sink-lock TTL stale-takeover. (Invariant 3)
Unattended contention/takeover ABORTS by default; Z_HARNESS_CLAIM_OVERRIDE=1 is explicit opt-in. Z_HARNESS_CLAIM_DISABLE=1 skips claiming entirely. (Invariant 4)
Holder string is the only carrier of identity: <session>::<run>::<command>. Colon in any field is rejected (exit 2) to preserve '::' delimiter unambiguity. (Invariant 6)
Session id is export-once AND persisted to archive/$RUN/session-id; restored on resume before every acquire call. plan-claim.sh never calls session-id itself. (Invariant 7)

acquire.0: acquired, self-reentry, or Z_HARNESS_CLAIM_DISABLE=1 — caller holds the lock (or disabled)
acquire.1: live-peer contention — holder JSON printed to stdout (best-effort, TOCTOU, display-only); caller does NOT hold lock
acquire.2: stale-takeover succeeded — caller NOW holds the lock; normal post-crash path
acquire.3: corrupt lock or invalid-holder/invalid-args — caller does NOT hold lock

heartbeat.0: refreshed, disabled, OR transient read error (heartbeat_error emitted, non-fatal)
heartbeat.9: confirmed lost claim — holder present-and-different or lock free; transient read failure is NOT exit 9

release.0: always (best-effort; --expected-holder guard prevents releasing a peer's lock)

Z_HARNESS_CLAIM_TTL_SECS.description: TTL seconds for claim liveness. Not a TOML key. Not emitted by export-env.

Z_HARNESS_CLAIM_OVERRIDE.description: Set to 1 to allow unattended runs to proceed through contention/stale-takeover/corrupt without aborting.

Z_HARNESS_CLAIM_DISABLE.description: Set to 1 to skip all claim locking. Every subcommand is an immediate exit-0 no-op. Release is a safe no-op regardless of event presence.

gotchas: exit-2 (stale-takeover) is the NORMAL post-crash recovery path, not a rare edge case. The setsid-detached daemon survives SIGKILL and leaks until TTL. Unattended default: abort unless Z_HARNESS_CLAIM_OVERRIDE=1.
The holder JSON printed by acquire (exit 1/2) and status is best-effort TOCTOU — re-read AFTER sink-lock returned. The gate keys on the exit code, not the JSON. Do not gate logic on JSON content.
Z_HARNESS_CLAIM_DISABLE=1: release is a safe no-op and is NOT gated on an acquire event being present. Callers always safe to call release regardless of this knob.

heartbeat exit 9 fires ONLY on confirmed ownership change (holder present-and-different, or lock free). A transient read/corrupt error is heartbeat_error + exit 0 (non-fatal). Do not conflate these two paths.

heartbeat BEFORE every AskUserQuestion is the load-bearing call — it extends TTL to survive the user-wait. The after-gate heartbeat (user_wait_end) is optional when the next phase heartbeat is imminent.
At exit-2 abort (stale-takeover, we hold the lock), release MUST be called before aborting. At exit-0/1/3 abort, do NOT call release (we never held the lock).
session-id persist+restore (Invariant 7) is required for the self-reentry guard to work on macOS. Without it, a resumed run sees its own prior claim as a foreign contender.
Z_HARNESS_CLAIM_TTL_SECS, Z_HARNESS_CLAIM_OVERRIDE, and Z_HARNESS_CLAIM_DISABLE are env-only. They are NOT in config.py DEFAULTS or VALIDATORS and are NOT emitted by export-env.

plan-claim.sh must pass --ttl-seconds to sink-lock read-holder so the stale flag is consistent with the TTL acquire uses. Omitting it causes read-holder to use sink-lock's default (7200), which can report stale:false for a slug that acquire would actually take over (2700 basis).
